        Args:
            title (str): Title for the bookmark (must be non-empty).
            url (str): URL to bookmark (must be valid format).
            folder_id (str): ID of the folder to contain this bookmark.
            tags (List[str]): List of tag_ids to associate.
            description (str, optional): Description of the bookmark.
            added_date (str, optional): Date when added (ISO8601 recommended), auto-set if not provided.

        Returns:
            dict:
                - success: True/False
                - message: Success message (if True)
                - error: Reason for failure (if False)

        Constraints:
            - Title must not be empty.
            - URL must be valid format.
            - Bookmark must not already exist in same folder with same URL.
            - Folder must exist.
            - Each tag in tags must exist in self.tags.
        """

        # Title check
        if not title or title.strip() == "":
            return { "success": False, "error": "Bookmark title must not be empty." }

        # Folder existence
        if folder_id not in self.folders:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Specified folder does not exist." }

        # URL format validation (simple regex for HTTP/HTTPS)
        url_pattern = r"^https?://[^\s]+$"
        if not re.match(url_pattern, url):
            return { "success": False, "error": "Bookmark URL is not valid." }

        # Duplicate check: same URL and folder
        for bm in self.bookmarks.values():
            if bm["url"] == url and bm["folder_id"] == folder_id:
                return { "success": False, "error": "Bookmark with this URL already exists in the specified folder." }

        # Tag existence check
        invalid_tags = [tag_id for tag_id in tags if tag_id not in self.tags]
        if invalid_tags:
            return { "success": False, "error": f"Invalid tag_ids: {', '.join(invalid_tags)}" }

        # Generate bookmark_id (simple unique by time and folder count)
        bookmark_id = f"bm_{len(self.bookmarks)+1}_{int(datetime.utcnow().timestamp())}"

        # Set added_date to now if not provided
        if not added_date:
            added_date = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()

        new_bookmark = {
            "bookmark_id": bookmark_id,
            "title": title,
            "url": url,
            "added_date": added_date,
            "folder_id": folder_id,
            "tags": tags,
            "description": description
        }

        self.bookmarks[bookmark_id] = new_bookmark

        return { "success": True, "message": "Bookmark added successfully." }

env_182_rl.environment_introduction:
A patient healthcare portal is a secure web-based system designed for patients to manage their health information and interact with medical providers.  
It stores personal details, medical records, appointment schedules, and allows secure document uploads for consultations.  
This environment naturally supports tasks like attaching medical files to upcoming appointments, ensuring privacy and streamlined communication between patients and clinics.

state_space_definition.description: Represents an individual patient using the portal.

state_space_definition.attributes: cord_id, patient_id, file_path, file_type, upload_datetime, description, access_permission
state_space_definition.description: Represents individual medical documents/files uploaded by or related to a patient.

state_space_definition.attributes: appointment_id, patient_id, provider_id, appointment_datetime, appointment_type, sta
state_space_definition.description: Represents scheduled consultations, including provider and time information.
Represents medical staff available for consultations.

constraints_rules: Only authorized patients can upload medical records for their own appointments.
Medical records must be securely stored and access-controlled.
Uploaded files must be associated with the correct appointment and patient.
Medical record file types and size may be subject to restrictions.
Patients and providers can only access records according to permission settings.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve details for a patient by patient_id or name.
Retrieve all scheduled appointments for a specified patient.
List a patient’s pending/upcoming appointments (optionally filtered by type).
Retrieve complete details of a specific appointment by appointment_id.
Retrieve provider details (name, specialization, contact info) by provider_id.
List all medical records uploaded by or related to a patient.
List all medical records associated with a specific appointment.
Check if a medical file’s type and size meet upload restrictions.
Determine if a patient/provider has permission to access/view a specific medical record.
Retrieve details about a single medical record by record_id.
Upload a new medical file for a patient, associating it to an appointment, enforcing file type/size restrictions and setting initial access permissions.
Link an existing medical record to a specific appointment (if not already associated).
Modify the access permissions of an existing medical record (e.g., allow provider to view).
Remove a medical record from the system (with access/restriction checks).
Edit metadata or description of an existing medical record (e.g., clarify its intended use for consultation).
Remove the association between a medical record and a specific appointment, if needed.

from typing import Dict, TypedDict
from typing import Optional, Dict
import datetime
import uuid



class PatientInfo(TypedDict):
    patient_id: str
    name: str
    contact_info: str
    date_of_birth: str
    login_credential: str

class MedicalRecordInfo(TypedDict):
    record_id: str
    patient_id: str
    file_path: str
    file_type: str
    upload_datetime: str
    description: str
    access_permission: str

class AppointmentInfo(TypedDict):
    appointment_id: str
    patient_id: str
    provider_id: str
    appointment_datetime: str
    appointment_type: str
    status: str

class ProviderInfo(TypedDict):
    provider_id: str
    name: str
    specialization: str
    contact_info: str

class PatientHealthcarePortal:
    def __init__(self, init_config: dict):
        """
        Environment state for the healthcare portal.
        init_config: external initializer (not implemented here).
        """
        # Patients: {patient_id: PatientInfo}
        self.patients: Dict[str, PatientInfo] = {}
        # MedicalRecords: {record_id: MedicalRecordInfo}
        self.medical_records: Dict[str, MedicalRecordInfo] = {}
        # Appointments: {appointment_id: AppointmentInfo}
        self.appointments: Dict[str, AppointmentInfo] = {}
        # Providers: {provider_id: ProviderInfo}
        self.providers: Dict[str, ProviderInfo] = {}

        # Constraints and access control:
        # - Only authorized patients can upload medical records for their own appointments
        # - Medical records must be securely stored and access-controlled
        # - Uploaded files must be associated with the correct appointment and patient
        # - Medical record file types and size may be subject to restrictions
        # - Patients and providers can only access records according to permission settings

        self.init_config = init_config

def upload_medical_record(
        self,
        patient_id: str,
        appointment_id: str,
        file_path: str,
        file_type: str,
        file_size: int,
        upload_datetime: str,
        description: str,
        access_permission: str
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Upload a new medical file for a patient for a given appointment.
        Enforces file type and size restrictions and sets initial access permissions.
    
        Args:
            patient_id (str): Patient uploading the record.
            appointment_id (str): Associated appointment.
            file_path (str): Path to uploaded file.
            file_type (str): The file extension/type.
            file_size (int): File size in bytes.
            upload_datetime (str): Upload timestamp (ISO string).
            description (str): Optional metadata for the record.
            access_permission (str): Initial access permission string.
    
        Returns:
            dict:
                success (bool): Whether upload succeeded.
                message (str): Description of success.
                or
                error (str): Reason for failure.
            
        Constraints:
            - Patient must exist.
            - Appointment must exist and belong to patient.
            - Only authorized patients can upload for their own appointments.
            - File type/size must be valid.
            - Medical record must be associated with patient and appointment.
        """
        # Patient existence/auth check
        patient = self.patients.get(patient_id)
        if not patient:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Patient does not exist." }

        appointment = self.appointments.get(appointment_id)
        if not appointment:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Appointment does not exist." }
        if appointment["patient_id"] != patient_id:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Appointment does not belong to patient, cannot upload." }

        # File type and size validity (assume helper is implemented)
        file_check_result = self.check_file_type_and_size_validity(file_type=file_type, file_size=file_size)
        if not file_check_result.get("success", False):
            return { "success": False, "error": f"File type/size invalid: {file_check_result.get('error', 'Unknown')}" }

        # Create a unique record_id
        record_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        if record_id in self.medical_records:
            # Extremely unlikely, but handle
            return { "success": False, "error": "Record ID collision, try again." }

        # Store MedicalRecordInfo
        record_info = MedicalRecordInfo(
            record_id=record_id,
            patient_id=patient_id,
            file_path=file_path,
            file_type=file_type,
            upload_datetime=upload_datetime,
            description=description,
            access_permission=access_permission
        )
        self.medical_records[record_id] = record_info

        # Here we could (optionally) store a mapping: appointment_id -> [record_id], but the schema doesn't enforce.

        return { "success": True, "message": "Medical record uploaded and associated." }

env_183_rl.environment_introduction:
This environment is a support group management system that tracks scheduled meetings, participant lists, meeting codes for access control, and venue details.  
It typically allows users to register or sign in, find relevant group meetings by topic, join sessions using meeting codes, and manage recurring event logistics.  
The environment maintains state about participants and their association with specific meetings, ensuring secure and organized group interactions.

state_space_definition.attributes: meeting_id, topic, schedule, venue, meeting_code, participants_list (participant_ids), recurrence_pattern
state_space_definition.description: Represents a support group meeting, its topic, occurrence details, access code, and participating users.
Represents an individual who attends support group meetings.
Tracks which participants joined which meetings, including attendance and history.
Physical location information for scheduled meetings.

constraints_rules: Only participants who provide the correct meeting_code may join the corresponding meeting.
Meeting participant lists are updated upon successful joining, and reflect current attendance.
Venue capacity must not be exceeded for any meeting.
Each meeting must have a unique meeting_code for access control.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve participant information given their name (e.g., Sarah).
Get full details of a participant using their participant_id.
List all registered participants in the system.
Search/return meetings (meeting_id, time, venue) matching a given topic.
Find meetings scheduled at a given time and venue.
Retrieve meeting details given a meeting_code.
Get details (topic, schedule, venue, capacity, participants, code) of a meeting by meeting_id.
List current participants in a given meeting.
Retrieve venue information using a street address.
Get venue details (address, room, capacity) by venue_id.
Query the capacity of the venue hosting a meeting.
Retrieve past attendance/join records for a given meeting.
Register a new participant in the system (e.g., Sarah if not already present).
Participant attempts to join a meeting (must provide correct code; system checks capacity and updates participant list/attendance).
Remove a participant from a meeting’s participant list and update attendance status.
Schedule a new meeting with topic, time, venue, recurrence, and unique code.
Update meeting information (topic, time, code, venue, etc.).
Add a new venue location into the system.
Change or update a participant’s registration status.
Delete a participant entirely from the system.

        participant_id: str,
        name: str,
        contact_info: str,
        registration_status: str = "registered"
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Register a new participant in the support group management system.

        Args:
            participant_id (str): Unique identifier for the participant.
            name (str): Name of the participant.
            contact_info (str): Contact details for the participant.
            registration_status (str): Registration status (default: "registered").

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": "Participant <name> registered successfully."
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": "Participant with ID <participant_id> already exists."
            }

        Constraints:
            - Participant ID must be unique in the system.
            - Participant registration_status defaults to "registered".
        """
        if participant_id in self.participants:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": f"Participant with ID {participant_id} already exists."
            }

        new_participant: ParticipantInfo = {
            "participant_id": participant_id,
            "name": name,
            "contact_info": contact_info,
            "registration_status": registration_status
        }

        self.participants[participant_id] = new_participant
        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"Participant {name} registered successfully."
        }

def create_meeting(
        self,
        topic: str,
        schedule: str,
        venue_id: str,
        recurrence_pattern: str,
        meeting_code: str
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Schedule a new meeting with topic, time, venue, recurrence, and unique code.

        Args:
            topic (str): The topic of the meeting.
            schedule (str): Date/time info for the meeting.
            venue_id (str): The venue's unique identifier.
            recurrence_pattern (str): Recurrence info (e.g., weekly, monthly).
            meeting_code (str): Access code (must be unique across meetings).

        Returns:
            dict:
                {
                    "success": True,
                    "message": "Meeting scheduled with meeting_id <id>."
                }
                or
                {
                    "success": False,
                    "error": str  # reason for failure
                }

        Constraints:
            - Venue must exist.
            - meeting_code must be unique.
            - participants_list is initialized empty.
            - meeting_id must be unique (auto-generate).
        """
        # Venue existence check
        if venue_id not in self.venues:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Venue does not exist."}

        # meeting_code uniqueness check
        for mtg in self.meetings.values():
            if mtg["meeting_code"] == meeting_code:
                return {"success": False, "error": "Meeting code already in use."}

        # Auto-generate meeting_id (simple increment or UUID)
        # We'll use integer as string from total count + 1, not production safe
        meeting_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

        meeting_info: MeetingInfo = {
            "meeting_id": meeting_id,
            "topic": topic,
            "schedule": schedule,
            "venue": venue_id,
            "meeting_code": meeting_code,
            "participants_list": [],
            "recurrence_pattern": recurrence_pattern
        }

        self.meetings[meeting_id] = meeting_info
        self.meeting_participants[meeting_id] = []

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": f"Meeting scheduled with meeting_id {meeting_id}."
        }

env_184_rl.environment_introduction:
This environment is a review management component within an e-commerce platform, where detailed records of products—including dietary supplements—are maintained with unique identifiers.  
Users submit reviews that are linked to products using these IDs, and the system persists, organizes, and exposes this data for retrieval and analysis.  
It naturally supports querying capabilities to fetch all reviews for any given product, fulfilling tasks related to consumer feedback and product reputation.

state_space_definition.description: Represents items offered on the platform, including dietary supplements, with unique identifiers.

state_space_definition.attributes: view_id, product_id, user_id, rating, review_text, timestamp, moderation_sta
state_space_definition.description: Represents consumer feedback submitted for products, linked to specific products and users.
Represents the author of reviews and facilitates tasks relating to user-generated content and moderation.

constraints_rules: Each review must be linked to an existing product via product_id.
Reviews can only be retrieved for products that exist in the system.
Reviews may be subject to moderation before being visible in queries (based on moderation_status).
Users may be limited to one review per product.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve product details using its product_id.
Retrieve full list of products in the system.
Retrieve all reviews attached to a given product by product_id.
Retrieve reviews for a product filtered by moderation_status (e.g., only "approved" reviews).
Retrieve details for a specific review given its review_id.
Retrieve user details using their user_id.
List all reviews authored by a specified user.
Check whether a given user has already reviewed a given product.
Submit a new review for a product by a user (enforcing one review per product per user constraint).
Change the moderation_status of a review (e.g., approve or reject).
Update the content, rating, or other fields of a submitted review.
Remove a review from the system.
Create a new product entry in the system.
Remove a product (and possibly its related reviews) from the system.
Register a new user in the system.
Remove a user (and possibly all their reviews) from the system.

def add_review(
        self,
        product_id: str,
        user_id: str,
        rating: int,
        review_text: str,
        timestamp: str,
        moderation_status: str
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Submit a new review for a product by a user.

        Enforces constraint: one review per product per user.

        Args:
            product_id (str): Target product's unique ID.
            user_id (str): User's unique ID.
            rating (int): Numerical rating for the product.
            review_text (str): The actual feedback text.
            timestamp (str): ISO string or similar representation of review time.
            moderation_status (str): Initial moderation status for the review.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": "Review added",
                "review_id": <str>
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": "Product/User doesn't exist, or user already reviewed product"
            }

        Constraints:
            - Product must exist.
            - User must exist.
            - One review per product per user.
            - Unique review_id per review.
        """

        if product_id not in self.products:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Product does not exist" }

        if user_id not in self.users:
            return { "success": False, "error": "User does not exist" }

        # Enforce one review per product/user
        for review in self.reviews.values():
            if review["product_id"] == product_id and review["user_id"] == user_id:
                return { "success": False, "error": "User has already reviewed this product" }

        # Generate unique review_id (simple increment or UUID-like)
        base_id = f"{product_id}-{user_id}"
        suffix = 1
        review_id = base_id
        while review_id in self.reviews:
            suffix += 1
            review_id = f"{base_id}-{suffix}"

        # Construct review info
        review_info: ReviewInfo = {
            "review_id": review_id,
            "product_id": product_id,
            "user_id": user_id,
            "rating": rating,
            "review_text": review_text,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "moderation_status": moderation_status
        }

        self.reviews[review_id] = review_info

        return {
            "success": True,
            "message": "Review added",
            "review_id": review_id
        }

env_185_rl.environment_introduction:
This environment is a personal contacts management system, such as an address book or contact app, which tracks and organizes detailed contact information for individuals and institutions.  
Entries include names, phone numbers, and categories (like emergency contacts), allowing users to add, modify, or remove records easily.  
State is maintained persistently, ensuring that updates like deleting information for "No.1 Hospital" are reflected in future interactions.

state_space_definition.attributes: contact_id, name, type (individual/institution), phone_numbers, addresses, emails, notes, catego
state_space_definition.description: Represents a person or organization whose information is maintained in the address book. Includes multiple kinds of contact information and classification by categories.
Represents a label or group which can be assigned to contacts to facilitate organization and filtering (e.g., "emergency", "medical", "family", etc.).

constraints_rules: Each contact must have a unique identifier.
Contacts can belong to multiple categories.
Deleting contact information must be persistent and irreversible unless there is an undo feature.
Some contacts may have missing fields (e.g., no email or address), but essential information (e.g., name or phone number) may be required.
Duplicate contact names are allowed but must be distinguishable via other attributes or contact_id.

Lookup a category's attributes using its name.

Assign an existing category to a contact.
Unassign a category from a contact.
Permanently remove a contact record from the system (irreversible unless undo is implemented).
Restore a previously deleted contact (if undo feature is supported).

Remove a category from the address book (and/or unassign it from any contacts).

from typing import Dict, List, TypedDict



class ContactInfo(TypedDict, total=False):
    contact_id: str
    name: str
    type: str  # 'individual' or 'institution'
    phone_numbers: List[str]
    addresses: List[str]
    emails: List[str]
    notes: str
    categories: List[str]  # category_id's assigned to this contact

class CategoryInfo(TypedDict):
    category_id: str
    category_name: str
    description: str

class PersonalContactsManagementSystem:
    def __init__(self, init_config: dict):
        # Contacts: {contact_id: ContactInfo}
        self.contacts: Dict[str, ContactInfo] = {}
        # Categories: {category_id: CategoryInfo}
        self.categories: Dict[str, CategoryInfo] = {}

        # constraints and rules:
        # - Each contact must have a unique identifier (contact_id)
        # - Contacts can belong to multiple categories
        # - Deleting contact information must be persistent and irreversible unless there is an undo feature
        # - Some contacts may have missing fields (e.g., no email or address); essential information (e.g. name or phone number) may be required
        # - Duplicate contact names are allowed but must be distinguishable via other attributes or contact_id

        self.init_config = init_config

def get_contacts_by_type(self, contact_type: str) -> dict:
        """
        Fetch all contacts that match the given type ('individual' or 'institution').

        Args:
            contact_type (str): The contact type ('individual' or 'institution').

        Returns:
            dict:
                success: True if operation successful, False otherwise
                data: List of matching ContactInfo dicts (may be empty)
                error: An error message if unsuccessful

        Constraints:
            - contact_type must be 'individual' or 'institution'
        """
        if contact_type not in {"individual", "institution"}:
            return {
                "success": False,
                "error": "Invalid contact type. Allowed values are 'individual' or 'institution'."
            }

        result = [
            contact
            for contact in self.contacts.values()
            if contact.get("type") == contact_type
        ]

        return {
            "success": True,
            "data": result
        }

def add_contact(
        self,
        contact_id: str,
        name: str,
        type: str,
        phone_numbers: list,
        addresses: list = None,
        emails: list = None,
        notes: str = "",
        categories: list = None
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Add a new contact record to the address book.

        Args:
            contact_id (str): Unique identifier for the new contact.
            name (str): Name of the contact. (Required)
            type (str): 'individual' or 'institution'. (Required)
            phone_numbers (list): List of phone numbers. (At least one required)
            addresses (list, optional): List of addresses.
            emails (list, optional): List of email addresses.
            notes (str, optional): Optional notes.
            categories (list, optional): List of category_id strings assigned to this contact.

        Returns:
            dict:
                success: True if the contact is added, with a success message.
                success: False and error message if failed due to input/constraints.

        Constraints:
            - contact_id must be unique.
            - name and at least one phone number are required.
            - Optional fields (addresses, emails, notes, categories) can be missing.
        """
        if contact_id in self.contacts:
            return { "success": False, "error": f"Contact ID '{contact_id}' already exists." }
        if not name or not isinstance(name, str):
            return { "success": False, "error": "Contact name is required and must be a string." }

            "type": type,
            "phone_numbers": phone_numbers,
            "addresses": addresses if addresses is not None else [],
            "emails": emails if emails is not None else [],
            "notes": notes if notes else "",
            "categories": categories if categories is not None else []
        }

        self.contacts[contact_id] = contact_info
        return { "success": True, "message": f"Contact '{contact_id}' added." }

def update_contact_info(
        self, 
        contact_id: str, 
        name: str = None, 
        type: str = None, 
        phone_numbers: List[str] = None, 
        addresses: List[str] = None, 
        emails: List[str] = None, 
        notes: str = None,
        categories: List[str] = None
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Edit the information of an existing contact identified by contact_id.

        Args:
            contact_id (str): Unique identifier of the contact to update.
            name (str, optional): Updated name of the contact.
            type (str, optional): Updated type ('individual' or 'institution').
            phone_numbers (List[str], optional): Updated phone number list.
            addresses (List[str], optional): Updated address list.
            emails (List[str], optional): Updated email list.
            notes (str, optional): Updated notes.
            categories (List[str], optional): Updated list of category_ids (must exist).

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "message": "Contact info updated"
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str
            }

        Constraints:
            - contact_id must exist.
            - Cannot update contact_id.
            - Categories (if provided) must exist in self.categories.
        """
        if contact_id not in self.contacts:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Contact does not exist" }

        contact = self.contacts[contact_id]

        # Check for new categories validity
        if categories is not None:
            missing_categories = [cat_id for cat_id in categories if cat_id not in self.categories]
            if missing_categories:
                return { 
                    "success": False, 
                    "error": f"These category IDs do not exist: {', '.join(missing_categories)}"
                }
            contact["categories"] = categories

        if name is not None:
            contact["name"] = name
        if type is not None:
            contact["type"] = type
        if phone_numbers is not None:
            contact["phone_numbers"] = phone_numbers
        if addresses is not None:
            contact["addresses"] = addresses
        if emails is not None:
            contact["emails"] = emails
        if notes is not None:
            contact["notes"] = notes

        # Persist the changes
        self.contacts[contact_id] = contact

        return { "success": True, "message": "Contact info updated" }

env_186_rl.environment_introduction:
This environment is a web-based support group platform designed for members to interact, share, and record their experiences.  
It maintains user accounts, group memberships, discussion threads, and journal entries, allowing for secure and private reflection or optional sharing within groups.  
Such a platform naturally facilitates the creation, storage, and retrieval of journal entries in the context of group support and community interaction.

state_space_definition.description: Represents an individual platform member with authentication and identification details.
Represents a group for support and interaction among members.
Represents a user's affiliation and role within a specific support group.

state_space_definition.attributes: ntry_id, user_id, group_id (nullable), content, timestamp, visibility
state_space_definition.description: Records a user's personal reflection, with optional sharing/visibility settings regarding group access.
Facilitates group conversations and shared discussions among members.

constraints_rules: Only users who are members of a support group may share journal entries within that group.
Journal entry visibility is controlled by user settings (private vs group-shared).
Group membership status (active, pending, removed) determines access rights to group content.
Discussion threads must belong to a valid support group.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve full information for a user by user ID (name, email, account status).
Retrieve details for a support group by group ID (name, description, privacy setting).
List all support groups to which a user is a member (with membership status).
Query and validate a user's membership status in a specific group (active, pending, removed).
Check that a given group exists and is valid for operation (e.g., not deleted).
List all members of a specific support group (with membership status).
Retrieve all journal entries authored by a particular user.
Retrieve all journal entries shared within a specific group.
Recover full information and visibility details for a specific journal entry.
Retrieve all discussion threads belonging to a support group.
Get title, creator, timestamp, and group for a discussion thread.
Add a new journal entry for a user, optionally associate it with a group, set content and visibility.
Change a journal entry's visibility setting (private or group-shared).
Establish a new support group (set name, description, privacy).
Add or update a membership record to reflect user's active role in a group.
Update the status of a user's membership in a group (activate, remove, set pending).
Start a new thread within a valid support group.
Remove a journal entry from the platform.
Remove a discussion thread from a group.
Modify the content of an existing journal entry.
Modify group description or privacy settings.

def get_support_group_info(self, group_id: str) -> dict:
        """
        Retrieve details (name, description, privacy setting) for a support group by group ID.

        Args:
            group_id (str): Unique identifier of the support group.

        Returns:
            dict:
                - success: True and data (SupportGroupInfo) if group exists.
                - success: False and error string if not found.

        Constraints:
            - If the specified group_id does not exist, returns failure.
        """
        group_info = self.groups.get(group_id)
        if not group_info:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Support group not found" }

        # Return all details for the support group
        return { "success": True, "data": group_info }

get_discussion_threads_in_group.source_code:
def get_discussion_threads_in_group(self, group_id: str) -> dict:
        """
        Retrieve all discussion threads that belong to a specified support group.

        Args:
            group_id (str): The ID of the support group.

        Returns:
            dict:
                - success: True and data: list of DiscussionThreadInfo (may be empty if no threads)
                - success: False and error: str (if the group does not exist)

        Constraints:
            - group_id must refer to a valid (existing) support group.
        """
        if group_id not in self.groups:
            return {"success": False, "error": "Support group does not exist"}

        result = [
            thread for thread in self.threads.values()
            if thread["group_id"] == group_id
        ]

        return {"success": True, "data": result}

env_187_rl.environment_introduction:
This environment is a specialized software system used in hospitals to organize and deliver patient meal services.  
It maintains records of patient profiles, including medical conditions and dietary restrictions, and coordinates meal schedules according to time and menu availability.  
Healthcare staff use this system to ensure meals are safe and appropriate for each patient, with dynamic queries supporting clinical care and food service needs.

state_space_definition.description: Represents a hospital patient, including relevant diet limitations and personal info.

state_space_definition.attributes: meal_id, name, description, dietary_properties (e.g. gluten-free), allergen_info
state_space_definition.description: Represents a meal available for service, including its compatibility with various restrictions.
Represents when and if a meal is available for delivery.
Represents users (e.g., dietitians, nurses) who interact with the system.

constraints_rules: Meal offerings must comply with each patient’s dietary restrictions and medical conditions.
Meal can only be assigned if it is available at the requested date and time.
Allergen information must be accurate and up-to-date for food safety.
Patients can only receive meals appropriate for current care protocols.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve full profile and dietary restrictions of a patient by patient_id.
List patients filtered by a specific medical condition (e.g., celiac disease).
Retrieve dietary restrictions for a specified patient.
Retrieve the full list of available meals in the system.
Get full meal details (properties, allergens) for a specified meal_id.
List meals matching certain dietary properties (e.g., gluten-free).
Filter meals by absence/presence of allergenic ingredients.
Retrieve meal schedule info for a specific date/time.
Return a list of meals available for a specific patient at a specified datetime, supporting dietary compatibility and schedule constraints.
List staff members filtered by their role (dietitian, nurse, etc.).
Assign a scheduled, compatible meal to a patient for a specific time.
Modify dietary restrictions for a patient profile.
Change dietary properties associated with a meal.
Modify the allergen info for food safety compliance.
Set or modify the availability status of a meal at a given time.
Add a new schedule entry for a meal (new time, availability).
Delete a scheduled meal time entry from the system.

        """
        if not isinstance(property, str) or not property.strip():
            return { "success": False, "error": "Invalid property value" }

        property = property.strip().lower()
        matched_meals = [
            meal for meal in self.meals.values()
            if any(prop.lower() == property for prop in meal.get("dietary_properties", []))
        ]

        return { "success": True, "data": matched_meals }

def get_meals_available_for_patient_at_datetime(self, patient_id: str, scheduled_datetime: str) -> dict:
        """
        Return a list of meals available for a specific patient at a specified datetime,
        satisfying schedule availability and dietary compatibility constraints.

        Args:
            patient_id (str): Unique identifier for the patient.
            scheduled_datetime (str): Datetime string (ISO format) for the meal.

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "data": List[MealInfo]  # List of meals matching constraints (may be empty)
            }
            or
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str
            }

        Constraints:
            - Patient must exist.
            - Only meals scheduled as 'available' for given datetime are considered.
            - Meals must satisfy patient's dietary_restrictions.
        """
        # Validate patient
        patient = self.patients.get(patient_id)
        if not patient:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Patient ID does not exist" }
        dietary_restrictions = patient.get("dietary_restrictions", [])
        # Collect compatible, available meals
        compatible_meals = []
        for meal_id, meal in self.meals.items():
            # Check scheduling: is meal available at scheduled_datetime?
            schedules = self.meal_schedules.get(meal_id, [])
            schedule_ok = any(
                sch["scheduled_datetime"] == scheduled_datetime and sch["availability_sta"] == "available"
                for sch in schedules
            )
            if not schedule_ok:
                continue
            # Dietary check: every restriction must be satisfied by meal properties
            meal_props = set(prop.lower() for prop in meal.get("dietary_properties", []))
            restrictions = set(r.lower() for r in dietary_restrictions)
            if not restrictions <= meal_props:
                continue
            # If passed both checks, add meal
            compatible_meals.append(meal)
        return { "success": True, "data": compatible_meals }

def remove_meal_schedule(self, meal_id: str, scheduled_datetime: str) -> dict:
        """
        Delete a scheduled meal time entry for a specific meal from the system.

        Args:
            meal_id (str): The unique identifier of the meal.
            scheduled_datetime (str): The ISO format datetime string for the schedule entry to remove.

        Returns:
            dict: On success:
                      {
                          "success": True,
                          "message": "Meal schedule removed successfully."
                      }
                  On failure:
                      {
                          "success": False,
                          "error": "reason for failure"
                      }

        Constraints:
            - Meal_id must exist in the system's schedule records.
            - A scheduled meal entry with the given datetime must exist to be removed.
        """
        # Check meal_id exists in meal_schedules
        if meal_id not in self.meal_schedules:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Meal ID does not exist in schedules." }
    
        # Find and delete the specified scheduled_datetime entry
        schedules = self.meal_schedules[meal_id]
        initial_len = len(schedules)

        # Filter out the schedule targeted for removal
        filtered_schedules = [entry for entry in schedules if entry["scheduled_datetime"] != scheduled_datetime]
    
        if len(filtered_schedules) == initial_len:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Scheduled meal entry not found for provided datetime." }
    
        # Update the schedules; if empty, that's fine.
        self.meal_schedules[meal_id] = filtered_schedules

        return { "success": True, "message": "Meal schedule removed successfully." }

env_188_rl.environment_introduction:
This environment consists of a centralized software platform used by gyms or fitness centers to track their fitness machines and equipment.  
Each machine has a unique identifier and associated records such as condition, location, maintenance history, and usage statistics.  
Staff use this system to quickly retrieve information about equipment status, ensuring timely maintenance and optimal facility operation.

state_space_definition.description: Represents an individual piece of fitness equipment tracked in the system.
Tracks usage data for each machine to inform maintenance and operational decisions.

state_space_definition.attributes: cord_id, machine_id, date, action_performed, staff_id, no
state_space_definition.description: Represents a historical record of maintenance activities for each machine.
Represents a physical area (room, zone) within the facility where machines are placed.
Represents staff members who may be assigned to maintenance activities.

constraints_rules: Each machine must have a unique machine_id.
A machine's condition must be one of predefined states (e.g., operational, requires maintenance, out of order).
Maintenance records must reference valid machine_ids and staff_ids.
Location assignments for machines must correspond to valid location_ids.

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve all info for a machine given its unique machine_id.
Query the current condition/status of a machine ("operational", "requires maintenance", "out of order").
Retrieve the complete list of fitness machines in the system.
Get all machines placed in a specified location (by location_id).
Retrieve usage data (hours, count, last used) for a specific machine.
Get all maintenance records associated with a given machine_id.
Get details about a specified facility location.
Get information on staff members by staff_id.
Retrieve all locations available within the facility.
Retrieve a list of all staff members registered in the system.
Change a machine's current_condition to a new allowed state.
Move a machine to a new location (location_id).
Create and store a new maintenance record for a machine, referencing valid staff.
Update attributes (notes, action, date) of an existing maintenance record.
Remove a maintenance record from the history.
Update usage hours, count, or last_used timestamp for a machine.
Add a new machine entry to the system (with unique machine_id).
Delete a machine from the system (in case of disposal).
Add a new equipment location to the system.
Modify details of an existing location.
Delete a location (if no machine is assigned).
Add a new staff member record to the system.
Edit info for a staff member.
Delete a staff member from the registry, if not referenced in maintenance records.

from typing import Dict, List, TypedDict, Optional



class MachineInfo(TypedDict):
    machine_id: str
    type: str
    model: str
    current_condition: str   # Should be one of: "operational", "requires maintenance", "out of order"
    location: str            # location_id

class UsageStatisticsInfo(TypedDict):
    machine_id: str
    usage_hours: float
    usage_count: int
    last_used: str           # ISO timestamp or date string

class MaintenanceRecordInfo(TypedDict):
    record_id: str
    machine_id: str
    date: str                # ISO timestamp or date string
    action_performed: str
    staff_id: str
    notes: Optional[str]     # Inferred from attribute "no"

class LocationInfo(TypedDict):
    location_id: str
    name: str
    description: str

class StaffInfo(TypedDict):
    staff_id: str
    name: str
    role: str
    contact_info: str

class FitnessEquipmentManagementSystem:
    def __init__(self, init_config: dict):
        """
        Environment for fitness equipment management and tracking.
        init_config: external initializer (not implemented here).
        """

        # Machine dictionary mapping machine_id to MachineInfo
        # State space: Machine (machine_id, type, model, current_condition, location)
        self.machines: Dict[str, MachineInfo] = {}

        # Usage statistics per machine_id
        # State space: UsageStatistics (machine_id, usage_hours, usage_count, last_used)
        self.usage_stats: Dict[str, UsageStatisticsInfo] = {}

        # Maintenance records indexed by record_id
        # State space: MaintenanceRecord (record_id, machine_id, date, action_performed, staff_id, notes)
        self.maintenance_records: Dict[str, MaintenanceRecordInfo] = {}

        # Locations indexed by location_id
        # State space: Location (location_id, name, description)
        self.locations: Dict[str, LocationInfo] = {}

        # Staff indexed by staff_id
        # State space: Staff (staff_id, name, role, contact_info)
        self.staff: Dict[str, StaffInfo] = {}

        # Constraints:
        # - Each machine must have a unique machine_id.
        # - current_condition must be in {"operational", "requires maintenance", "out of order"}.
        # - Maintenance records must reference valid machine_ids and staff_ids.
        # - Machine location assignment must correspond to valid location_ids.

        self.init_config = init_config

add_staff.source_code:
def add_staff(
        self,
        staff_id: str,
        name: str,
        role: str,
        contact_info: str
    ) -> dict:
        """
        Add a new staff member to the system.

        Args:
            staff_id (str): Unique identifier for the staff member.
            name (str): Human-readable staff name.
            role (str): Staff role (e.g., technician, manager).
            contact_info (str): Contact information for the staff member.

        Returns:
            dict:
                - On success:
                    {
                        "success": True,
                        "message": "Staff member added successfully."
                    }
                - On failure:
                    {
                        "success": False,
                        "error": str  # Reason for failure
                    }

        Constraints:
            - staff_id must be unique (cannot already exist).
            - All fields should be non-empty strings.
        """
        # Validate unique staff_id
        if staff_id in self.staff:
            return { "success": False, "error": "Staff ID already exists." }

        # Basic validation for input fields
        if not all(isinstance(f, str) and f.strip() for f in [staff_id, name, role, contact_info]):
            return { "success": False, "error": "All fields must be non-empty strings." }

        staff_info = {
            "staff_id": staff_id,
            "name": name,
            "role": role,
            "contact_info": contact_info
        }
        self.staff[staff_id] = staff_info
        return { "success": True, "message": "Staff member added successfully." }

This environment consists of a mobile or web-based application where users log health metrics such as weight, symptoms, and milestones throughout their pregnancy.  
It maintains historical records, computes averages, and integrates medical guidelines to provide personalized recommendations.  
Such an app enables users to track progress, receive health insights, and compare their statistics to standard ranges suitable for each pregnancy stage.

from typing import Dict, List, TypedDict, Optional
import datetime



class UserInfo(TypedDict):
    _id: str
    name: str
    date_of_birth: str
    height: float
    pre_pregnancy_weight: float
    due_date: str
    pregnancy_start_date: str  # Corrected attribute name

class HealthMetricLogInfo(TypedDict, total=False):
    log_id: str
    user_id: str
    timestamp: str
    weight: float
    symptoms: List[str]
    notes: Optional[str]  # Corrected attribute name and made optional

class PregnancyStageInfo(TypedDict):
    _id: str
    current_week: int
    current_trimester: int  # Corrected attribute name

class GuidelineInfo(TypedDict):
    age_identifier: str
    recommended_min_gain: float
    recommended_max_gain: float
    description: str

class PregnancyTrackingHealthManagementApp:
    def __init__(self, init_config: dict):
        """
        Pregnancy tracking and health management app environment.
        init_config: customizable initializer placeholder (not implemented).
        """

        # Users: {_id: UserInfo}
        # Entity: User | Attributes: _id, name, date_of_birth, height, pre_pregnancy_weight, due_date, pregnancy_start_date
        self.users: Dict[str, UserInfo] = {}

        # Health Metric Logs: {log_id: HealthMetricLogInfo}
        # Entity: HealthMetricLog | Attributes: log_id, user_id, timestamp, weight, symptoms, notes
        self.health_logs: Dict[str, HealthMetricLogInfo] = {}

        # Pregnancy Stages: {_id: PregnancyStageInfo}
        # Entity: PregnancyStage | Attributes: _id, current_week, current_trimester
        self.pregnancy_stages: Dict[str, PregnancyStageInfo] = {}

        # Guidelines: {age_identifier: GuidelineInfo}
        # Entity: Guideline | Attributes: age_identifier, recommended_min_gain, recommended_max_gain, description
        self.guidelines: Dict[str, GuidelineInfo] = {}

        # Constraints:
        # - Health metrics must be associated with valid users.
        # - Pregnancy stage is computed from due date or pregnancy start date.
        # - Guideline recommendations vary by pregnancy stage (week or trimester).
        # - Weight gain calculations are based on pre-pregnancy weight and logged weights.
        # - Medical guidelines must be sourced from authoritative references.

        self.init_config = init_config

def list_guidelines(self) -> dict:
        """
        Retrieve all available medical guidelines for different pregnancy stages.

        Args:
            None

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "data": List[GuidelineInfo]  # All guideline records (may be empty)
            }

        Constraints:
            - No input required; simply returns all guidelines.
        """
        guidelines_list = list(self.guidelines.values())
        return { "success": True, "data": guidelines_list }

env_190_rl.environment_introduction:
This environment is a secure Electronic Health Record (EHR) system used by healthcare organizations to store, retrieve, and manage patient data.  
It maintains structured records for each patient, including demographics, medical history, allergies, laboratory results, and current medications.  
The system provides authorized users, such as clinicians and staff, with tools to quickly search and verify allergy information, making it a natural setting for allergy queries like checking for Penicillin sensitivity.

state_space_definition.description: Represents an individual whose health data is stored and managed in the EHR system.
Represents a specific allergy entry for a patient, including the allergen (e.g., Penicillin) and the nature of the reaction.

state_space_definition.attributes: patient_id, medication_name, dosage, start_date, end_date, prescribing_clinician
state_space_definition.description: Tracks the medicines currently or previously prescribed to a patient.
Stores the results of medical lab tests performed for a patient.
Represents healthcare staff with permissions to access and modify patient data in the EHR system.

constraints_rules: Only authorized users may view or modify patient health records.
Each allergy entry must be associated with a specific patient and substance.
Patient data is kept secure and confidential in compliance with health privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA).
The system ensures a unique patient identity via patient_id.

operation_list.operation_description: Determine whether a user (by user_id) has rights to access or modify the given patient’s record.
Retrieve details about an authorized user (name, role, access rights).
Retrieve complete demographic and medical history for a patient by patient_id.
Search for patient(s) using demographic information (name, date_of_birth, etc.).
Retrieve all allergy records associated with a specific patient.
Query allergy records for a patient filtered by substance (e.g., Penicillin).
Fetch full details (reaction, confirmation, date) for a patient’s specific allergy record.
List all patients in the EHR system (admin/query use).
Retrieve medication history records for a patient.
Fetch all laboratory results for a patient.
Add a new allergy record for a patient, specifying substance, reaction type, and confirmation status.
Modify an existing allergy entry (e.g., updating confirmation status or reaction).
Remove an allergy entry from a patient’s record.
Add a new authorized user to the system with specified access rights.
Change the access permissions of a system user.
Remove an authorized user from the system.

verify_user_authorization.doc:
Determine whether a user (by user_id) has rights to access or modify the given patient’s record.

Args:
    user_id (str): ID of the user attempting to access/modify the record.
    patient_id (str): ID of the patient whose data is being accessed.
    action (str): Requested action; valid values are 'view' or 'modify'.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "authorized": bool,
        "details": str  # explanation if authorized/denied
    }
    or {
        "success": False,
        "error": str   # reason for failure
    }

Constraints:
    - Only users in authorized_users may access patient data.
    - The user must have relevant rights for requested action.
    - Patient must exist (identity via patient_id).
    - Supported actions: 'view', 'modify'

env_191_rl.environment_introduction:
The environment is a personal nutrition tracking application that allows users to log meals, calories, and consumption times.  
It maintains a stateful database of meal records linked to users, supporting queries, trends, and progress tracking over time.  
This setup naturally facilitates detailed logging and analysis of food intake and makes it easy to record and reference information like the "chicken salad" meal described in the task.

state_space_definition.description: Represents the person using the app and linking all meal records.
Stores details of each logged meal, including its nutritional value and time of consumption.

constraints_rules: Each MealRecord must be linked to a specific User.
Calorie values for a meal must be non-negative.
consumed_at must be a valid timestamp.
Meal names should be descriptive but are otherwise flexible (no duplicate restrictions).

operation_list.operation_description: Retrieve user information using the user's name.
Retrieve user information using the user's unique _id.
List all registered users in the app.
Retrieve all meal records linked to a specific user.
Retrieve all meal records for a user in a specific time/date interval.
Search for meal records of a user matching a meal name.
Retrieve details of a specific meal record by record_id.
Aggregate total calories and meal counts for a user over a given period.
Create and store a new MealRecord for a user, with meal name, calorie value, and consumption time (validates constraints).
Modify details of an existing MealRecord (e.g., calories, meal name, consumed_at).
Remove a meal record from the app for a user.
Add multiple meal records simultaneously for a user.
Update the consumed_at timestamp of a meal record to ensure validity.
Update the calorie value of an existing meal record (ensures non-negative value).

def list_all_users(self) -> dict:
        """
        List all registered users in the nutrition tracking app.

        Args:
            None

        Returns:
            dict: {
                "success": True,
                "data": List[UserInfo],  # List of all users' info (may be empty)
            }

        Constraints:
            - No constraints; returns all UserInfo in the system.
            - If no users are registered, returns an empty list (not an error).
        """
        all_users = list(self.users.values())
        return { "success": True, "data": all_users }
